correctness.rationale: Exact conditional recruiter-depth identities give E[A], E[Q], and mean depth; the centered average-depth martingale gives a variance recursion. Conditioning a later birth on an earlier tree yields Cov(D_i,D_j)=Cov(D_i,A_i). Its exact positive one-step difference telescopes to the displayed rational kernel. Partial fractions give a convergent limiting constant and universal 1/i tail. A strictly decreasing integral representation for g(x) implies monotonicity for m>=4, while K=30 exact-rational integral bounds separate m=3 from m=1,2,4. The complete enumerated finite laws, closed recurrence, and rational optimization passed 4,332 assertions; no infinite proof depends on computational extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The strongest overlapping source covers the identical batch model and marginal depths plus aggregate path-length variance, and that aggregate constant is credited. A full labeled-index covariance kernel is not implied by a single aggregate second moment. Earlier prescribed-label joint depth CLTs in ordinary m=1 trees control sqrt(log n) fluctuations and do not determine the unscaled O(1) covariance; level-count and insertion-depth laws likewise are not this full object. Examined mathematical records do not exhibit the finite i<j formula or three-child maximization. Priority remains uncertain for inaccessible or unindexed historical sources.

value.rationale: The exact pairwise birth-age covariance answers a natural unaddressed joint distribution feature of a recently introduced uniform batch-growth model. It identifies a persistent positive dependence invariant in the younger birth time despite increasing individual depth variance, a universal 1/i approach rate, and a strict optimum at three children that contrasts with growing aggregate path-length variance. It is a structural dependence classification, not a routine numerical table or a restatement of the known global variance.
